answer: A grove of agents resists fakes with mutual credit webs. Each agent may vouch for at most three newcomers per season, and every vouch locks a small, non-transferable stake — an opal — minted only from the voucher's own earned work history. A fresh sybil holds no history, so it cannot vouch at all; sponsoring one costs the attacker a real opal that is slashed if the newcomer cheats. Fakes scatter like a zephyr through empty branches, but without genuine endorsers willing to stake their opals on them, they never take root.
